1.overview: John the Baptist prepares the way for Jesus, who is baptized, declared God’s beloved Son, and tempted in the wilderness. After John’s arrest, Jesus proclaims God’s kingdom in Galilee, calls disciples, teaches and heals with authority, and cleanses a leper whose report draws crowds.

2.overview: In Capernaum, Jesus heals a paralytic and asserts the Son of Man’s authority to forgive sins, then calls Levi and eats with tax collectors and sinners. He explains why his disciples do not fast and, after the Pharisees challenge their Sabbath actions, cites David and declares the Son of Man Lord of the Sabbath.

sections.heading: The Sabbath and the Son of Man

3.overview: Jesus heals a man on the Sabbath, prompting the Pharisees and Herodians to plot against him, then draws crowds from surrounding regions and appoints twelve apostles. He answers the scribes’ accusation that he drives out demons by Beelzebul and identifies those who do God’s will as his family.

4.overview: Jesus teaches beside the sea through parables of the sower, the lamp, and the growing and mustard seeds, explaining the kingdom of God and varied responses to the word. Later, he stills a storm on the sea as he crosses with his disciples, who question his authority over the wind and water.

sections.heading: The Sower and the Purpose of Parables

5.overview: In the region of the Gerasenes, Jesus drives a legion of demons from a man into a herd of pigs, and the restored man proclaims what Jesus has done throughout the Decapolis. Back across the sea, Jesus heals a woman who touches his cloak and raises Jairus’s daughter from the dead.

sections.heading: The Gerasene Man and the Legion

6.overview: Jesus faces rejection in Nazareth, sends the Twelve to preach and heal, and Herod orders John the Baptist’s execution. Jesus feeds five thousand, walks on the sea to the disciples, and heals the sick throughout Gennesaret.

sections.heading: Feeding the Crowd and Walking on the Sea

7.overview: Pharisees and scribes challenge Jesus over ritual washing, and he condemns traditions that nullify God’s commands before teaching that defilement comes from within the heart. In the region of Tyre, Jesus casts a demon from a Syrophoenician woman’s daughter, then in the Decapolis heals a deaf man who can hardly speak.

8.overview: Jesus feeds four thousand people, refuses the Pharisees’ demand for a sign, and questions the disciples about their understanding of the loaves and the leaven. At Bethsaida he heals a blind man, Peter identifies him as the Christ, and Jesus teaches about his coming suffering, death, and resurrection, then describes the cost of following him and the Son of Man’s coming in glory.

sections.heading: Suffering and the Cost of Discipleship

9.overview: Jesus is transfigured before Peter, James, and John, explains Elijah’s coming, and casts a spirit out of a boy after the disciples fail to do so. In Galilee and Capernaum, he predicts his death and resurrection, teaches the Twelve about service and welcoming others, and warns against causing believers to stumble and against sin.

10.overview: In Judea beyond the Jordan, Jesus teaches about divorce, welcomes children, and tells a wealthy man that following him requires giving up his possessions, while explaining the difficulty of wealth and the rewards of leaving things for the gospel. On the road to Jerusalem, he predicts his death and resurrection, teaches the Twelve that greatness means serving others, and restores Bartimaeus’s sight near Jericho.

sections.heading: The Rich Man and the Kingdom
Jesus Predicts His Death and Teaches Service

11.overview: Jesus enters Jerusalem to acclaim from the crowd, inspects the temple, and later curses a fruitless fig tree before driving buyers and sellers from the temple courts. After the tree withers, he teaches about faith, prayer, and forgiveness, then refuses to disclose his authority to Jerusalem’s religious leaders when they will not answer his question about John’s baptism.

sections.heading: The Fig Tree and the Temple

12.overview: Jesus tells the parable of the vineyard tenants and answers challenges from the Pharisees, Herodians, Sadducees, and a scribe about taxes, resurrection, and the greatest commandment. In the temple courts, He questions how the Christ can be David’s son, warns against the scribes, and says the poor widow gives more than the wealthy because she contributes all she has.

sections.heading: The Parable of the Vineyard Tenants
The Greatest Commandment and David’s Lord
Warnings About Scribes and the Widow’s Offering

13.overview: Jesus predicts the temple’s destruction and answers Peter, James, John, and Andrew with warnings about deception, conflict, persecution, and tribulation. He describes the coming of the Son of Man and the gathering of the elect, then teaches that the time is unknown and calls for watchfulness.

sections.heading: Tribulation and the Coming of the Son of Man
The Unknown Time and the Call to Watch

14.overview: As the Passover approaches, a woman anoints Jesus at Bethany, Judas agrees to betray him, and Jesus shares the Passover meal with his disciples, predicting his betrayal, their flight, and Peter’s denial. In Gethsemane Jesus prays before Judas leads an armed crowd to arrest him; the high priest’s council condemns him, while Peter denies knowing him three times.

15.overview: The chief priests and Sanhedrin hand Jesus over to Pilate, who releases Barabbas and condemns Jesus to crucifixion. Jesus is mocked and crucified at Golgotha, dies as the temple veil is torn, and is buried by Joseph of Arimathea while women witness where he is laid.

16.overview: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome find Jesus’ tomb open, where a young man announces that Jesus has risen and tells them to inform the disciples. The risen Jesus appears to Mary Magdalene, two followers, and the Eleven, commissions the Eleven to proclaim the gospel, and is taken up into heaven as they preach with signs accompanying their work.

sections.heading: The Women Find the Empty Tomb
The Ascension and the Disciples’ Mission
